summary: Since May 2026 visitors to Chad who are not exempt must apply for an e-Visa on the official platform evisa.td — a visa issued outside it after 21 May 2026 is not valid for entry. Citizens of the CEMAC states and of the other countries and territories on the platform's exemption list enter without a visa. The UK FCDO advises against all travel to the north, the Lake Chad region and the border areas, and against all but essential travel to the rest of the country.

tips.text: The UK FCDO advises against all travel to the northern provinces (Borkou, Ennedi Ouest, Ennedi Est and Tibesti), western Kanem Province, the Lake Chad region and within 30 km of Chad’s other borders, and against all but essential travel to the rest of the country, including N’Djamena. It says the Chad–Sudan border is closed to travellers, with limited humanitarian exceptions.

Chad's immigration service says visas issued outside evisa.td after 21 May 2026 are invalid. The platform says you cannot apply more than 90 days before arrival, recommends applying at least 7 days ahead, does not refund fees and cannot correct an e-Visa once issued.

If you stay in Chad more than 72 hours, the UK FCDO says you must register with the police at the Commissariat Central (police headquarters) on Avenue General Kerim Nassour; bring a passport photograph.

The Government of Canada says a government permit is required for all photography in Chad, that photographing airports, military establishments and government buildings is prohibited, and that cameras may be confiscated without notice.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Chad?
faq.answer: Yes, unless your passport is exempt. Chad's e-Visa platform lists Barbados, Benin, Bermuda, the Central African Republic, Congo, the Cook Islands, Dominica, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, Gambia, Malaysia, Mali, Micronesia, Niger, Nigeria, Rwanda, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, Singapore, Suriname and Togo. Cameroon is not on that list, but the CEMAC Additional Act of 25 June 2013 lets citizens of all CEMAC states, Cameroon included, enter without a visa and stay up to 90 days. Everyone else applies online at evisa.td.

faq.question: Does Chad have an eVisa?
faq.answer: Yes, and it is now the only way to get one. Since 11 May 2026 every visa application is made on evisa.td (diplomatic and courtesy visas excepted), and a visa issued outside the platform after 21 May 2026 does not allow entry. You cannot apply more than 90 days before arrival, and the platform recommends applying at least 7 days ahead. A new fee grid has been announced, but the platform does not publish the amounts.

faq.question: Is Chad safe for tourists?
faq.answer: The UK FCDO advises against all travel to the northern provinces (Borkou, Ennedi Ouest, Ennedi Est and Tibesti), western Kanem Province, the Lake Chad region and within 30 km of the other borders, and against all but essential travel to the rest of the country, including N'Djamena.

faq.question: Do I have to register after arriving in Chad?
faq.answer: Yes — the UK FCDO says that if you stay more than 72 hours you must register with the police, that the immigration officer will tell you to go to the Commissariat Central (police headquarters) on Avenue General Kerim Nassour, and that you must bring a passport photograph.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever vaccination for Chad?
faq.answer: Yes. Chad's e-Visa platform tells applicants to bring proof of yellow fever vaccination, which immigration checks on arrival.
